question: does RR-style stable per-thread slowdown (--chaos-per-thread-slowdown) lower seeds-to-reproduce vs plain --chaos?

feature.semantics: each thread gets a factor stable for the whole run (pure fn of sched_seed+dettid), log-uniform in [1/R,R], scaling the MEAN chaos timeslice length only (out-of-band budget; does NOT scale guest-visible virtual time). --strict-safe / L2-preserving.

workload.oracle: sha256 of hermit-filtered guest output; distinct sigs = distinct benign progress-tick interleavings
workload.race_class: benign multithreaded progress-tick (proxy for schedule-exploration power)
workload.caveat: only ~2 reachable interleavings at coarse timeslice + short thread runtimes; a WEAK test of the feature's thesis (which targets long, many-thread runs where per-timeslice priority redraw averages out).

results_headline: coarse regime: per-thread slowdown gives a slight edge (stf_med 2->1, hit 45%->50-52%) but stays in the 2-state binary (can't manufacture interleavings that don't exist); differences are within 40-seed noise. Fine timeslice (1e4) dominates either way (100% hit); adding slowdown slightly LOWERS diversity (36->26 distinct) because longer mean slices insert fewer preemption points. No regression; feature is correct, deterministic, L2-safe.
